name: jev-questions
how_to_use: Each group is one JEV request. The packer sends the group's state slice as the state and only the fields type, instructions and criteria of each question; viewpoint, status, ask, why and cadence are for people.

status: live means every label the question reads is built today; shadow means a forecast with no right answer at ask time, logged and never acted on; it is not graded, only the two sums are, never acted on; dark means the packer never asks it and the phone never counts it, because the source it needs is not plugged in (the news questions, until a news engine exists; dark_was keeps the status they return to).

Grading is of the two sums only, next_30 and next_60 in questions/sndk_hour.json, each by the bars at its own mark, as the phone shows them: blended half and half with the time-of-day odds (sndk_jev/clock.py), with JEV's own sums and the odds scored beside them. No live question is graded against the next move; a live question's weight is how well its fresh picks tracked the 30-minute band.

cadence is the starting interval. The service snaps it to 30, 60 or 120 minutes, recounts it each day from the day before, and holds the last fresh answer in between. Scans two minutes apart are 0.918 correlated on this name, so few questions gain from being asked more often than every read.
Read the probabilities from every score question, never its single score, which is a weighted mean and can sit between two levels.

Every threshold is written into the criteria in the words the label uses, because JEV cannot compare numbers. The 0.12 and 0.30 sigma bands are measured on this name at 30 minutes, on 5,815 thirty-minute windows: the end move is within 0.12 sigma 59% of the time and 0.30 is the 90th percentile of the furthest point.

retired lists the questions taken out, the day, the reason and the question that absorbed each one, if any; a retired question is never asked and its weight history stays in state/jev/ for the record.

price_recent_direction.ask: Over the last 30 minutes, did price rise, fall, or go nowhere?
price_recent_direction.why: It is the gate every momentum question hangs on, and it moves within the next 30 minutes.
price_recent_direction.instructions: Read `price.recent_move`. Which describes price over the last 30 minutes?

criteria.rising: price moved up by more than 0.15 sigma over the last 30 minutes
criteria.falling: price moved down by more than 0.15 sigma over the last 30 minutes
criteria.going_nowhere: price stayed within 0.15 sigma of where it was 30 minutes ago
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

price_in_day_range.ask: Is price near the top, the middle, or the bottom of today's range?
price_in_day_range.why: The best-spread check in the set, so it anchors how well JEV reads a plain label.
price_in_day_range.instructions: Read `price.day_range_position`. Where is price in today's range so far?

criteria.top: price is in the top third of today's range so far
criteria.middle: price is in the middle third of today's range so far
criteria.bottom: price is in the bottom third of today's range so far
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

price_vs_vwap.ask: Is price above, below, or at the day's average price?
price_vs_vwap.why: Where price sits against the day's average is the plainest read of who has been winning today.
price_vs_vwap.instructions: Read `price.vs_vwap`. Where is price compared with the day's volume-weighted average price?

criteria.above: price is more than 0.15 sigma above the average
criteria.below: price is more than 0.15 sigma below the average
criteria.at_it: price is within 0.15 sigma of the average
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

range_vs_normal.ask: Is today's range small, normal, or large for this time of day?
range_vs_normal.why: It says whether today is a quiet day or a big one, which changes how far any target is. The label names 3, 4 or 5 sessions early in the record; the criteria said five, and JEV read 9 of 12 such sentences right until the wording followed the label (12 of 12).
range_vs_normal.instructions: Read `range.today_vs_normal`. How does today's range so far compare with the prior sessions the label names, at this time of day?

criteria.small: today's range so far is in the bottom third of the last sessions at this time of day, however many sessions the label names
criteria.normal: today's range so far is in the middle third of the last sessions at this time of day, however many sessions the label names
criteria.large: today's range so far is in the top third of the last sessions at this time of day, however many sessions the label names
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

box_break_follow_through.ask: Where is price against the first half hour's range: inside all day, back inside after a break, or broken out and extending, stalling or fading?
box_break_follow_through.why: Absorbs box_status (2026-09-25): the old inside option held both 'inside all day' and 'back inside after a break', and JEV read back-inside sentences as a live break (3 of 12 right); with the two inside options split it read 40 of 40. It carries no forward value either way (Brier +0.0015 against the time of day), so it stays as the one description of the day's opening range. It needs the last 30 minutes' move, which does not exist while the box is still forming, so the question is first asked once the box has closed and has no forming option.
box_break_follow_through.instructions: Read `range.box_status` for where price is against the opening box, and `price.recent_move` for the last 30 minutes. A price that sits inside the box counts as inside, whatever it did earlier or over the last 30 minutes; only a price that sits beyond an edge now counts as broken. Which situation is it?

criteria.broke_up_extending: price has broken above the opening box, and over the last 30 minutes price rose more than 0.15 sigma
criteria.broke_up_stalling: price has broken above the opening box, and over the last 30 minutes price stayed within 0.15 sigma of where it was
criteria.broke_up_fading: price has broken above the opening box, and over the last 30 minutes price fell more than 0.15 sigma
criteria.broke_down_extending: price has broken below the opening box, and over the last 30 minutes price fell more than 0.15 sigma
criteria.broke_down_stalling: price has broken below the opening box, and over the last 30 minutes price stayed within 0.15 sigma of where it was
criteria.broke_down_fading: price has broken below the opening box, and over the last 30 minutes price rose more than 0.15 sigma
criteria.inside_all_day: price is inside the opening box and has stayed inside it all day
criteria.back_inside_after_a_break: price is inside the opening box, and earlier today it broke above the box, below it, or out both ways, and came back inside
criteria.unsure: the labels conflict or say too little to call

iv_trend.ask: Is the size of move the options market is pricing rising, falling, or flat over the last 30 minutes?
iv_trend.why: Rising implied volatility means the options market is pricing a bigger move, and it changes within the next 30 minutes.
iv_trend.instructions: Read `iv.trend_30min`. What has implied volatility done over the last 30 minutes?

criteria.rising: implied volatility rose by more than 2 vol points
criteria.falling: implied volatility fell by more than 2 vol points
criteria.flat: implied volatility stayed within 2 vol points of where it was
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

iv_skew.ask: Are puts or calls priced richer?
iv_skew.why: Which side is paid up for is a read on where the crowd wants protection, but it barely moves intraday, so ask it hourly.
iv_skew.instructions: Read `iv.skew`. Which side is priced richer in implied volatility? The sentence's opening words decide; the vol-point figure that follows is description, not the verdict.

criteria.puts_richer: the label opens 'puts carry a higher implied volatility than calls at equal distance'
criteria.calls_richer: the label opens 'calls carry a higher implied volatility than puts at equal distance'
criteria.about_even: the label opens 'puts and calls carry about the same implied volatility'; the signed vol-point figure after that is ignored
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

realized_vs_priced.ask: Over the last 30 minutes, did price move less than, about as much as, or more than the options market prices for 30 minutes?
realized_vs_priced.why: Replayed on 663 reads over 20 days (2026-08-26 to 09-24): after quieter than priced the next 30 minutes ended flat 70% of the time against 42% after about as priced, and the label beat the time of day alone on 13 of 20 days and against 20 of 20 shuffles; wilder than priced is almost only the first hour, where it adds nothing.
realized_vs_priced.instructions: Read `iv.vs_realized_30`. Over the last 30 minutes, did price move less than, about as much as, or more than the move the options market prices for 30 minutes?

criteria.quieter_than_priced: price's realized movement over the last 30 minutes was under the 0.7-times cut of the move the options market prices for 30 minutes, so quieter than priced
criteria.about_priced: price's realized movement over the last 30 minutes was between the 0.7-times and 1.3-times cuts of the move the options market prices for 30 minutes, so about as priced
criteria.wilder_than_priced: price's realized movement over the last 30 minutes was over the 1.3-times cut of the move the options market prices for 30 minutes, so wilder than priced
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

realized_vs_priced.proposed: 2026-09-25, from the 25-agent pressure test of 2026-09-24; see questions/proposals/2026-09-24-pressure-test.json

weight_side.ask: Does most of the options weight sit above price, below it, or evenly?
weight_side.why: The only strike question that varies day to day; graded as agreement with the label, never against the next move.
weight_side.instructions: Read `gex.weight_side`. Where does most of the options weight sit compared with price? The sentence's opening words decide: 'most of the options weight sits above price' is above, 'most ... sits below price' is below, 'split about evenly' is even; the percentage that follows is description, not the verdict.

criteria.above: the label opens with 'most of the options weight sits above price'; the percentage after that is ignored
criteria.below: the label opens with 'most of the options weight sits below price'; the percentage after that is ignored
criteria.even: the label opens with 'the options weight is split about evenly'; the percentage after that is ignored
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

volume_now.ask: Is trading heavy, normal, or light for this time of day?
volume_now.why: Volume against the same clock slot on prior days is the core of your second viewpoint.
volume_now.instructions: Read `volume.now`. Is trading heavy, normal or light for this time of day?

criteria.heavy: volume is in the top fifth for this time of day
criteria.normal: volume is in the middle band for this time of day
criteria.light: volume is in the bottom fifth for this time of day
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

volume_vs_before.ask: Did volume pick up with the move, stay heavy throughout, fade, or never pick up?
volume_vs_before.why: The label names two bands, one for the move and one for before it; naming every combination lets JEV match words instead of ranking two bands, which it cannot do.
volume_vs_before.instructions: Read `volume.on_move`. It names a volume band for the last 30 minutes, the move, and a band for the 30 minutes before the move began. Which situation is it?

criteria.picked_up: volume during the move is in the top fifth for its time of day, and volume before the move began was in the middle band or the bottom fifth
criteria.heavy_throughout: volume during the move is in the top fifth for its time of day, and volume before the move began was also in the top fifth
criteria.faded: volume during the move is in the middle band or the bottom fifth, and volume before the move began was in the top fifth
criteria.no_pickup: volume during the move is in the middle band or the bottom fifth, and volume before the move began was also in the middle band or the bottom fifth
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

pace_vs_before.ask: Is the last 10 minutes' move bigger, smaller, or the same as the 10 before?
pace_vs_before.why: Whether a move is speeding up or fading is the earliest sign it is about to end.
pace_vs_before.instructions: Read `momentum.pace`. Compared with the 10 minutes before it, is the last 10 minutes' move bigger, smaller or about the same?

criteria.bigger: the last 10 minutes moved more than 1.5 times as far as the 10 minutes before
criteria.smaller: the last 10 minutes moved less than two thirds as far as the 10 minutes before
criteria.about_the_same: the last 10 minutes moved between two thirds and 1.5 times as far as the 10 minutes before
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

fresh_action.ask: Is today's options trading fresh and one-sided, or is it positions left over from before?
fresh_action.why: New money leaning one way is a different board from yesterday's positions sitting still, and the current set cannot tell them apart.
fresh_action.instructions: Read `options.turnover` for today's contracts traded against the standing open position, and `options.call_put_split` for whether they were calls or puts. What is today's options trading doing?

criteria.fresh_calls: today's contracts traded are between 1 and 3 times, or more than 3 times, the standing open position, and mostly calls beyond the 60% cut
criteria.fresh_puts: today's contracts traded are between 1 and 3 times, or more than 3 times, the standing open position, and mostly puts, calls under the 40% cut
criteria.fresh_mixed: today's contracts traded are between 1 and 3 times, or more than 3 times, the standing open position, and an even split within 40% to 60%
criteria.standing_book: today's contracts traded are under 1 times the standing open position
criteria.unsure: the labels conflict or say too little to call

structure_survives_expiry.ask: Does today's strike structure carry into next week, or does it go with this week's expiry?
structure_survives_expiry.why: Decides whether holding overnight means holding into the same structure or a different one.
structure_survives_expiry.instructions: Read `gex.expiry_roll` for whether the later-dated book defends the same strikes as today's, on the call side and the put side, and `options.next_week_share` for the share of contracts that went to next week. Does the structure the book defends today carry into the later-dated book?

criteria.carries: BOTH the call side and the put side say the later-dated book defends the same strike as today's book, AND the share going to next week is a meaningful share, above the 25% cut
criteria.expires_with_this_week: either side says the later-dated book defends a different strike from today's book, or the share going to next week is a small share, under the 25% cut
criteria.unsure: the labels conflict or say too little to call

wall_return.ask: Is the nearest strike with a big pile of options close to price, and how often has price visited it today?
wall_return.why: `air_to_wall` read heavy_strike_close on 10 of 53 runs today, every one of them a strike price had come back to 0 or 1 times, and on the 43 open_air runs `range.wall_retests` moved through 0, 1, 2 and 4 visits (four visits to the call wall at 11:17, none to the put wall that replaced it at 11:31). The count is visits, the first arrival included; its sentence said 'come back' until 2026-09-25.
wall_return.instructions: Read `gex.air_to_wall` for how far the nearest heavy strike sits from price, and `range.wall_retests` for how many times price has visited that strike today, its first arrival included; the count is for the nearest heavy strike as the side packet last knew it, and it starts again when a different strike becomes the nearest. Which situation is it?

criteria.close_first_visit: the nearest heavy strike sits within 0.5 sigma of price, and price has visited it none or once today, counting its first arrival
criteria.close_worked: the nearest heavy strike sits within 0.5 sigma of price, and price has visited it two or more times today, counting its first arrival
criteria.far_worked: the nearest heavy strike sits more than 0.5 sigma from price, and price has visited it two or more times today, counting its first arrival
criteria.far_untouched: the nearest heavy strike sits more than 0.5 sigma from price, and price has visited it none or once today, counting its first arrival
criteria.no_wall: no heavy strike sits within reach
criteria.unsure: the labels conflict or say too little to call

wall_return.proposed: 2026-09-22, from the day's answers; see questions/proposals/2026-09-22.json

book_shift.ask: Since the options book last changed, did the nearest strike with a big pile of options on either side move, did the single heaviest strike move, or did nothing move?
book_shift.why: `gex.since_last_book` is built on every row that has an earlier book today and read by nothing, so a board that just re-drew its walls reads the same to JEV as one that stood still.
book_shift.instructions: Read `gex.since_last_book`. It says, for the heaviest strike, the nearest call wall and the nearest put wall, whether each is the same strike as at the last book, a different strike, or appeared or disappeared since. What moved?

criteria.walls_moved: the label says the nearest call wall or the nearest put wall is a different strike from the last book, or appeared or disappeared since the last book
criteria.heaviest_moved: the label says the heaviest strike now is a different strike from the last book, and both the nearest call wall and the nearest put wall are the same strike as at the last book
criteria.steady: the label says the heaviest strike, the nearest call wall and the nearest put wall are each the same strike as at the last book
criteria.unsure: the label says a strike could not be compared, or gives too little to call

todays_volume_location.ask: Where is today's option trading concentrated: at a strike above price, below it, at the nearest strike, or spread out?
todays_volume_location.why: Today's trading by strike, where the weight question reads the standing book.
todays_volume_location.instructions: Read `options.new_activity`. Where does the busiest strike sit?

criteria.above_price: the label says the busiest strike today sits above price, holding more than a fifth of the day's option volume
criteria.below_price: the label says the busiest strike today sits below price, holding more than a fifth of the day's option volume
criteria.at_price: the label says the busiest strike today is the one nearest price, holding more than a fifth of the day's option volume
criteria.spread_out: the label says today's option volume is spread across strikes, no strike holding more than a fifth
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

volume_backs_move.ask: Is volume backing the current move?
volume_backs_move.why: Volume and price action held together is your second viewpoint in one question, and the first that needs four sentences read at once.
volume_backs_move.instructions: Read `price.recent_move` for whether price rose or fell more than the move rule, `volume.on_move` for the volume band during the move and the band before it began, `volume.by_direction` for which way the volume leaned, and `momentum.closes` for the bar closes. Is the current move backed by volume?

criteria.backed: price rose or fell more than the 0.15 sigma move rule, volume during the move is in the top fifth and volume before the move began was in the middle band or the bottom fifth, and the volume printed leaning up beyond the 60% cut for a rise, or leaning down with up-minutes under the 40% cut for a fall
criteria.not_backed: price rose or fell more than the 0.15 sigma move rule, but volume during the move is in the middle band or the bottom fifth, or volume before the move began was also in the top fifth, or the volume printed against the move, leaning down for a rise or leaning up for a fall, or even within 40% to 60%
criteria.no_move: the labels say the last 30 minutes moved under the 0.15 sigma move rule, so there is no move to judge
criteria.unsure: the labels conflict or say too little to call

heavy_volume_location.ask: Is today's heaviest trading below price, above it, or right here?
heavy_volume_location.why: Where the day's volume actually traded is the half of volume and price action that a total never shows.
heavy_volume_location.instructions: Read `volume.at_price`. Where does the heaviest-volume stretch of the day sit relative to price?

criteria.below_price: the heaviest-volume stretch of the day sits below price
criteria.above_price: the heaviest-volume stretch of the day sits above price
criteria.at_price: the heaviest-volume stretch of the day includes the current price
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

move_retracement.ask: Of the last 30 minutes' move, how much has already been given back?
move_retracement.why: The sum picked down at 10:56, 11:00 and 11:17 on `price.recent_move` reading a fall of 0.24 to 0.27 sigma, while the unread `momentum.pauses` sentence said that fall had already given back more than all of itself at 10:56, 69% at 11:00 and 47% at 11:17.
move_retracement.instructions: Read `price.recent_move` for whether price rose or fell more than the move rule over the last 30 minutes, and `momentum.pauses` for how much of that move was given back at its deepest pullback. Which situation is it?

criteria.held: price rose or fell more than the 0.15 sigma move rule over the last 30 minutes, and the deepest pullback gave back less than a quarter of the move
criteria.given_back: price rose or fell more than the 0.15 sigma move rule over the last 30 minutes, and the deepest pullback gave back more than a quarter of the move but not all of it
criteria.fully_reversed: price rose or fell more than the 0.15 sigma move rule over the last 30 minutes, and the deepest pullback gave back all of the move or more
criteria.no_move: the labels say the last 30 minutes moved under the 0.15 sigma move rule, so there is no move and no pullback to judge
criteria.unsure: the labels conflict or say too little to call

move_retracement.proposed: 2026-09-22, from the day's answers; see questions/proposals/2026-09-22.json

move_vs_volume_shelf.ask: Is price moving away from the day's heaviest trading, moving back toward it, or sitting on it?
move_vs_volume_shelf.why: `heavy_volume_location` and `price_recent_direction` were both answered at full confidence on every read today but never in one sentence: from 10:17 to 11:17 the heaviest stretch sat 0.1 to 0.6 sigma above price while price fell away from it, at 12:00 price rose back toward it, and from 12:31 to the close the stretch included price and price stalled.
move_vs_volume_shelf.instructions: Read `volume.at_price` for where the day's heaviest-volume stretch sits relative to price, and `price.recent_move` for what price did over the last 30 minutes. Which situation is it?

criteria.leaving_upward: the heaviest-volume stretch of the day sits below price, and over the last 30 minutes price rose more than 0.15 sigma
criteria.leaving_downward: the heaviest-volume stretch of the day sits above price, and over the last 30 minutes price fell more than 0.15 sigma
criteria.returning: the heaviest-volume stretch of the day sits above price and over the last 30 minutes price rose more than 0.15 sigma, or it sits below price and price fell more than 0.15 sigma
criteria.holding_away: the heaviest-volume stretch of the day sits above or below price, and over the last 30 minutes price stayed within 0.15 sigma of where it was
criteria.sitting_on_it: the heaviest-volume stretch of the day includes the current price
criteria.unsure: the labels conflict or say too little to call

move_vs_volume_shelf.proposed: 2026-09-22, from the day's answers; see questions/proposals/2026-09-22.json

volume_profile_thickness.ask: Is price sitting in a thin, middling or thick part of today's volume profile?
volume_profile_thickness.why: Replayed on 661 reads over 20 days (2026-08-26 to 09-24): price stayed inside the 30-minute flat band 62% of the time in a thick part of the day's volume profile against 42% in a middling and 55% in a thin part, and it beat the time of day alone on 14 of 20 days and against 19 of 20 shuffles; the smoothed profile was the third of three cuts tried, so it is re-checked after ten more sessions.
volume_profile_thickness.instructions: Read `volume.at_price_thickness`. Is price sitting in a thin, middling or thick part of today's volume profile?

criteria.thick: the current price sits in a thick part of today's volume profile: its stretch traded at or above the 50% cut of the day's heaviest stretch
criteria.middling: the current price sits in a middling part of today's volume profile: its stretch traded between the 25% and 50% cuts of the day's heaviest stretch
criteria.thin: the current price sits in a thin part of today's volume profile: its stretch traded under the 25% cut of the day's heaviest stretch
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

volume_profile_thickness.proposed: 2026-09-25, from the 25-agent pressure test of 2026-09-24; see questions/proposals/2026-09-24-pressure-test.json

two_day_position.ask: Is price above both of the last two days' highs, below both lows, or in between?
two_day_position.why: Your third viewpoint word for word, and nothing in the current set reads yesterday's levels.
two_day_position.instructions: Read `price.vs_yesterday` and `price.vs_day_before`. Where is price against the last two sessions' highs and lows?

criteria.above_both_highs: price is more than 0.15 sigma above yesterday's high and above the high of the day before
criteria.below_both_lows: price is more than 0.15 sigma below yesterday's low and below the low of the day before
criteria.between: price is inside the range of at least one of the last two sessions
criteria.unsure: the labels conflict or say too little to call

prior_level_tested.ask: Has price tested one of yesterday's levels today?
prior_level_tested.why: Where price has touched is the half of your third viewpoint that a position alone does not give.
prior_level_tested.instructions: Read `range.prior_level_touches`. Has price spent at least one minute within reach of yesterday's high, low or close today?

criteria.true: price has spent one minute or more within reach of at least one of yesterday's high, low or close today
criteria.false: price has spent no minutes within reach of any of yesterday's high, low or close today

day_high_returns.ask: At the top of today's range, has price come back to the day's high since setting it?
day_high_returns.why: The day's high is where a rally is tested. Counted as returns since the high was set (the side packet's first visit is the setting touch itself, so the count used to read one too high), 168 service reads over 2026-09-04 to 09-24 split 37 at the top untested, 19 at the top and returned, 112 not at the top, so none-against-some keeps both answers alive where the old once-against-repeatedly cut did not. Replaces day_high_pressure on 2026-09-25, so its learning starts fresh.
day_high_returns.instructions: Read `price.day_range_position` for where price sits in today's range so far, and `range.high_retests` for how many times price has come back to the day's high since setting it. Which situation is it?

criteria.top_untested: price is in the top third of today's range so far, and price has come back to the day's high 0 times since setting it, none
criteria.top_returned: price is in the top third of today's range so far, and price has come back to the day's high once, or two or more times, since setting it
criteria.not_at_top: price is in the middle third or the bottom third of today's range so far
criteria.unsure: the labels conflict or say too little to call

momentum_stretched.ask: Is momentum stretched, and which way?
momentum_stretched.why: The 1-minute RSI read between on 95% of moments; the 5-minute RSI plus how long an extreme has held is the honest version of your fourth viewpoint.
momentum_stretched.instructions: Read `momentum.rsi_5min` for the 5-minute RSI, and `momentum.stretch` for how long the 1-minute RSI has held an extreme. Is momentum stretched?

criteria.stretched_up: the 5-minute RSI is above 70, and the 1-minute RSI has held an extreme for between 3 and 10 minutes or longer than 10 minutes
criteria.stretched_down: the 5-minute RSI is below 30, and the 1-minute RSI has held an extreme for between 3 and 10 minutes or longer than 10 minutes
criteria.not_stretched: the 5-minute RSI is between 30 and 70, or no extreme is being held, or it has held for under 3 minutes
criteria.unsure: the labels conflict or say too little to call

priced_hotter_than_next_week.ask: Is the size of move the options market is pricing for this week above, below, or level with next week's?
priced_hotter_than_next_week.why: Tells you whether today is priced as unusually hot, which sizes what an option costs to hold through it.
priced_hotter_than_next_week.instructions: Read `iv.term_slope`. How does this week's at-the-money implied volatility compare with next week's?

criteria.hotter: this week's at-the-money implied volatility sits above next week's, more than the 2 point flat band
criteria.cooler: this week's at-the-money implied volatility sits below next week's, more than the 2 point flat band
criteria.level: this week's and next week's at-the-money implied volatility are within the 2 vol point flat band, whichever week the label says is higher
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

vwap_slope.ask: Is the day's average price drifting higher, lower, or flat over the last 30 minutes?
vwap_slope.why: The direction the average itself is moving is the trend behind the where-is-price-against-it read.
vwap_slope.instructions: Read `momentum.vwap_slope`. Over the last 30 minutes, which way has the day's volume-weighted average price drifted?

criteria.drifting_higher: the day's average price has drifted higher over the last 30 minutes by more than the 0.05 sigma flat cut
criteria.drifting_lower: the day's average price has drifted lower over the last 30 minutes by more than the 0.05 sigma flat cut
criteria.flat: the day's average price has stayed within the 0.05 sigma flat cut over the last 30 minutes
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

stall_vs_vol.ask: While price is stalled, is the size of move the options market is pricing rising, falling, or flat?
stall_vs_vol.why: On all nine reads from 11:31 to the close `activity_state` said quiet (the last real move 20 to 161 minutes old) while `iv_trend` kept changing underneath it: rising at 12:31, 13:31 and 14:18, falling at 11:31, 12:00 and 14:00, flat at 13:00, 15:02 and 15:31.
stall_vs_vol.instructions: Read `context.time_since_last_move` for how long ago price last made a real move of 0.15 sigma within 10 minutes, and `iv.trend_30min` for what at-the-money implied volatility did over the last 30 minutes. Which situation is it?

criteria.stalled_vol_rising: price last made a real move 10 minutes ago or longer, and at-the-money implied volatility rose, more than the 2 point flat band, over the last 30 minutes
criteria.stalled_vol_falling: price last made a real move 10 minutes ago or longer, and at-the-money implied volatility fell, more than the 2 point flat band, over the last 30 minutes
criteria.stalled_vol_flat: price last made a real move 10 minutes ago or longer, and at-the-money implied volatility stayed within the 2 vol point flat band over the last 30 minutes
criteria.tape_moving: price last made a real move under 10 minutes ago, whatever implied volatility did
criteria.unsure: the labels conflict or say too little to call

stall_vs_vol.proposed: 2026-09-22, from the day's answers; see questions/proposals/2026-09-22.json

path_efficiency.ask: Over the last 30 minutes, did price travel cleanly, in a mixed way, or choppily?
path_efficiency.why: How much of the last 30 minutes' travel was net movement; the five-bar closes question only sees the last five minutes.
path_efficiency.instructions: Read `momentum.path_efficiency`. Which band does it name?

criteria.orderly: the label says path efficiency is orderly, 60% or more
criteria.mixed: the label says path efficiency is mixed, between 30% and 60%
criteria.choppy: the label says path efficiency is choppy, under 30%
criteria.no_move: the label says price stayed within the 0.15 sigma move rule, so there is no path to judge
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

vol_vs_price_direction.ask: Over the last 30 minutes, which way did price go and which way did the size of move the options market is pricing go?
vol_vs_price_direction.why: Pairs the options market's priced move with price direction; the stall question pairs it with a stall instead. Code decides which pairs fit.
vol_vs_price_direction.instructions: Read `price.recent_move` and `iv.trend_30min`. Which pairing is it?

criteria.fall_vol_rising: price fell more than the 0.15 sigma move rule, and at-the-money implied volatility rose by more than 2 vol points
criteria.rise_vol_falling: price rose more than the 0.15 sigma move rule, and implied volatility fell by more than 2 vol points
criteria.rise_vol_rising: price rose more than the 0.15 sigma move rule, and implied volatility rose by more than 2 vol points
criteria.fall_vol_falling: price fell more than the 0.15 sigma move rule, and implied volatility fell by more than 2 vol points
criteria.vol_flat: implied volatility stayed within the 2 vol point flat band, whatever price did
criteria.no_move: price stayed within the 0.15 sigma move rule and implied volatility moved more than 2 vol points
criteria.unsure: the labels conflict or say too little to call

week_position.ask: Is price in new ground above the week, new ground below it, or inside it?
week_position.why: Price against its own recent past is the spatial half of your fifth viewpoint; the label carries the distance to both edges of the week.
week_position.instructions: Read `price.multi_day_position`. Where is price against the last five sessions?

criteria.new_ground_above: price is above the last five sessions' high
criteria.new_ground_below: price is below the last five sessions' low
criteria.inside_the_week: price is between the last five sessions' low and high
criteria.unsure: the labels conflict or say too little to call

activity_state.ask: Is the market active right now, in price or in options, or quiet?
activity_state.why: How long since price last really moved, with how far into the session we are, is the time half of your fifth viewpoint; since 2026-09-25 a burst of options flow counts as active too. That moved 22 of 663 replayed reads from quiet to active (burst reads ended the next 30 minutes flat 38% of the time against 67% for a quiet options pace) and beat the price-only question on 14 of 20 days; it rests on 22 reads, so it is re-scored after ten more sessions.
activity_state.instructions: Read `context.time_since_last_move`, `context.session_progress`, `price.minute_width` and `options.flow_pace`. A burst of options flow counts as active even when price is still. Is the market active or quiet right now?

criteria.active: price last made a real move under 10 minutes ago, or this minute's range is wider than the 2-times cut, or options flow since the last options book is a burst, above the 1-times cut
criteria.quiet: price last made a real move 10 minutes ago or longer, this minute's range is within the 2-times cut, and options flow since the last options book is steady or quiet, not a burst, or there is no options pace to judge yet
criteria.unsure: the labels conflict or say too little to call

activity_state.proposed: 2026-09-25, the options arm from the 25-agent pressure test of 2026-09-24; see questions/proposals/2026-09-24-pressure-test.json

session_shape.ask: So far today, is the session rising, falling, flat, or has it reversed?
session_shape.why: The whole day's shape; the opening box question only says what happened against the first half hour.
session_shape.instructions: Read `range.session_shape`. Which shape does it name?

criteria.rising: the label says the session is rising: price is more than the 0.30 sigma cut above the open
criteria.falling: the label says the session is falling: price is more than the 0.30 sigma cut below the open
criteria.flat: the label says the session is flat: price is within the 0.30 sigma cut of the open
criteria.reversed_down: the label says the session has reversed down: price rose above the open then gave back a good part of it, past the 0.30 sigma cut
criteria.reversed_up: the label says the session has reversed up: price fell below the open then recovered a good part of it, past the 0.30 sigma cut
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

segment_vs_session.ask: Is the last 30 minutes continuing the day's move, reversing it, or pausing?
segment_vs_session.why: The same continue-or-reverse read as the opening box question, but against the whole day's shape.
segment_vs_session.instructions: Read `range.session_shape` for the session's shape and `price.recent_move` for the last 30 minutes. A session that is rising or has reversed up counts as rising; one that is falling or has reversed down counts as falling. Which pairing is it?

criteria.continuing: the session is rising and price rose more than the 0.15 sigma move rule in the last 30 minutes, or the session is falling and price fell more than the 0.15 sigma move rule
criteria.reversing: the session is rising and price fell more than the 0.15 sigma move rule in the last 30 minutes, or the session is falling and price rose more than the 0.15 sigma move rule
criteria.pausing: the session is rising or falling and price stayed within the 0.15 sigma move rule over the last 30 minutes
criteria.no_session_move: the session is flat, whatever the last 30 minutes did
criteria.unsure: the labels conflict or say too little to call

nearest_level_action.ask: At the nearest price level, did price cross it, cross and come back, sit within reach of it, or is nothing close?
nearest_level_action.why: One verdict at the one nearest level (the day's average price, the day's high or low, yesterday's levels, a wall), where the existing questions each watch one level.
nearest_level_action.instructions: Read `range.nearest_level`. What did price do at the nearest level over the last 30 minutes?

criteria.crossed_up: the label says price crossed the level from below in the last 30 minutes and is above it
criteria.crossed_down: the label says price crossed the level from above in the last 30 minutes and is below it
criteria.crossed_and_back: the label says price pushed through the level in the last 30 minutes and is back on the side it started
criteria.within_reach_above: the label says the level is above price within the 0.15 sigma reach, untouched in the last 30 minutes
criteria.within_reach_below: the label says the level is below price within the 0.15 sigma reach, untouched in the last 30 minutes
criteria.near_but_untouched: the label says the level is beyond the 0.15 sigma reach but within 0.5 sigma, untouched in the last 30 minutes
criteria.no_level_close: the label says no level is within 0.5 sigma of price
criteria.unsure: the label gives too little to call

news_kind.ask: What kind of item is this: a reported event, a price recap, or opinion?
news_kind.why: Sorting short text into a bounded answer is JEV's documented core use, and a price recap or a promo should never be read as news.
news_kind.instructions: Read `news.headline` and `news.excerpt`. What kind of item is this?

criteria.reported_event: the item reports something that happened or was announced, such as results, a deal, a product, a rating change or an index change
criteria.price_recap: the item only describes how the stock price moved
criteria.opinion_or_promo: the item is an opinion, a prediction by a non-official, or promotion
criteria.unsure: the item says too little to call

news_subject.ask: What is the news about: the whole market, SanDisk, its industry, or something else?
news_subject.why: Code decides relevance from the subject, so an item about the wrong company never reaches the reaction questions.
news_subject.instructions: Read `news.headline` and `news.excerpt`. What is the news about?

criteria.whole_market: the news moves most large US companies at once, such as interest rates, inflation, jobs data, tariffs or a war
criteria.sandisk: the news is about SanDisk's own business, such as results, products or management
criteria.memory_or_storage_industry: the news is about the memory or storage industry, or about a supplier, customer or competitor of SanDisk
criteria.index_or_fund_flows: the news is about SanDisk's place in an index, an ETF or fund holdings
criteria.something_else: the news is about something with no link to SanDisk, its industry or the market
criteria.unsure: the item says too little to call

news_is_new.ask: Does it report something new, or repeat what was already out?
news_is_new.why: Already-known news is the first way an item gets discounted.
news_is_new.instructions: Read `news.headline` and `news.recent_headlines`. Does `news.headline` report a new event, figure or decision, rather than repeat or comment on `news.recent_headlines`?

criteria.true: the headline reports a new event, figure or decision
criteria.false: the headline repeats or comments on what the recent headlines already report

news_reverses_earlier.ask: Does it deny, correct, or reverse an earlier report?
news_reverses_earlier.why: A reversal is new even when its words are old, and a plain is-it-new check would miss it.
news_reverses_earlier.instructions: Read `news.headline` and `news.recent_headlines`. Does `news.headline` deny, correct or reverse something reported in `news.recent_headlines`?

criteria.true: the headline denies, corrects or reverses something the recent headlines reported
criteria.false: the headline adds to or repeats the recent headlines, or reports something unrelated to them

news_direction.ask: Does the news point to lower prices, higher prices, both, or neither?
news_direction.why: The sign of the news is the one thing code cannot read from text; grade it against a human label, never against the next move.
news_direction.instructions: Read `news.headline` and `news.excerpt`. For holders of SanDisk, does this news point to lower prices, higher prices, both, or neither?

criteria.lower: the news gives holders a reason to expect lower prices for SanDisk
criteria.higher: the news gives holders a reason to expect higher prices for SanDisk
criteria.both: the news gives reasons to expect both lower and higher prices for SanDisk
criteria.neither: the news gives no reason to expect a price change for SanDisk
criteria.unsure: the item says too little to call

news_vs_expectation.ask: Did the news beat, miss, or match what was expected?
news_vs_expectation.why: Whether a result beat or missed is the second half of is-it-priced-in, and it is a reading of two texts rather than a number comparison.
news_vs_expectation.instructions: Read `news.headline` and `news.excerpt`, and compare what they report with `news.expectation`. Did the news beat, miss or match the expectation?

criteria.beat: the news reports a better result, guidance or outcome for SanDisk than `news.expectation` describes
criteria.miss: the news reports a worse result, guidance or outcome for SanDisk than `news.expectation` describes
criteria.in_line: the news reports a result, guidance or outcome that matches what `news.expectation` describes
criteria.unsure: the news and the expectation are about different things, or say too little to compare

news_size.ask: Because of this news, how far does price wander in the next 30 minutes?
news_size.why: Unsigned, so it is gradeable against the furthest point reached; asked twice, the gap between the two answers is what price has already done.
news_size.instructions: Read `news.headline`, `news.excerpt`, `news.age` and `news.price_reaction`. How far from where it is now does price get, at its furthest point in either direction, during `context.horizon`, because of this news?
criteria: because of this news, price stays within 0.12 sigma of where it is now the whole time
because of this news, price gets between 0.12 and 0.30 sigma away at its furthest point
because of this news, price gets more than 0.30 sigma away at its furthest point

news_reaction_ladder.ask: Because of this news, where does price end up in an hour?
news_reaction_ladder.why: Direction and size in one ladder; logged and graded by the bars, never acted on, because direction forecasts measured worthless on this name.
news_reaction_ladder.instructions: Read `news.headline`, `news.excerpt`, `news.age` and `news.price_reaction`. Because of this news, where does price end up at the end of `context.horizon`, compared with where it is now?
criteria: because of this news, price ends more than 0.30 sigma below where it is now
because of this news, price ends between 0.12 and 0.30 sigma below where it is now
because of this news, price ends within 0.12 sigma of where it is now
because of this news, price ends between 0.12 and 0.30 sigma above where it is now
because of this news, price ends more than 0.30 sigma above where it is now

move_size.ask: How far does price wander from here in the next 30 minutes, either way?
move_size.why: The one forecast that is unsigned and gradeable, so it tells you whether the labels carry any information at all.
move_size.instructions: Read `price.recent_move`, `volume.now`, `momentum.pace`, `iv.trend_30min`, `iv.expected_move_used`, `range.today_vs_normal`, `range.box_status` and `gex.air_to_wall`. How far from where it is now does price get, at its furthest point in either direction, during `context.horizon`?
criteria: price stays within 0.12 sigma of where it is now the whole time
price gets between 0.12 and 0.30 sigma away at its furthest point
price gets more than 0.30 sigma away at its furthest point

direction_lean.ask: At the end of the next 30 minutes, is price above here, below here, or about where it is?
direction_lean.why: Direction was measured worthless on this name over 391 readings; this stays as a shadow forecast, asked as an outcome rather than a tally of labels, which JEV cannot count.
direction_lean.instructions: Read `price.recent_move`, `price.vs_vwap`, `price.day_range_position`, `volume.now`, `gex.weight_side` and `gex.air_to_wall`. At the end of `context.horizon`, where is price compared with where it is now?

criteria.above: price ends more than 0.12 sigma above where it is now
criteria.below: price ends more than 0.12 sigma below where it is now
criteria.flat: price ends within 0.12 sigma of where it is now
criteria.unsure: the labels say too little to call

nearest_strike_reached.ask: Within the next 30 minutes, does price trade at or through the nearest strike with a big pile of options?
nearest_strike_reached.why: SNDK PRO measured that heavy strikes do not draw price on this name; keeping the claim as a forecast lets the grading loop keep testing it instead of anyone assuming it.
nearest_strike_reached.instructions: Read `gex.air_to_wall` for the nearest heavy strike, and `price.recent_move`, `momentum.pace` and `price.day_range_position` for how price is moving. During `context.horizon`, does price trade at or through that nearest heavy strike?

criteria.true: at some point during the next 30 minutes price trades at or through the nearest heavy strike named in the label
criteria.false: price stays short of the nearest heavy strike for the whole of the next 30 minutes

retired.why: a day-level constant that leans with the move since the close; no forward value (Brier +0.0084 against the time of day, better on 8 of 20 days)
retired.ask: Are the options positions market makers hold much bigger, smaller, or about the same as at yesterday's close?

retired.why: one-sided: thin_or_scattered on 62 of 62 live asks; no forward value (+0.0052, 5 of 20 shuffles)
retired.ask: Is there a band of neighbouring strikes with big piles of options near price, and on which side?

retired.why: the front-week at-the-money quote shows 1x1 lots, so the lean is noise, and it can never be graded offline
retired.ask: On the at-the-money option, is more size showing on the buy side, on the sell side, or about even?

retired.why: even on 82% of service reads; no forward value (+0.0086, 3 of 20 shuffles); nothing beyond iv_skew
retired.ask: Is the day's expected move skewed down, skewed up, or even?

retired.why: a duplicate: NMI 0.78 with volume_backs_move and 0.70 with price_recent_direction; JEV said unsure on every quiet read
retired.ask: How many of the last five bars closed in the direction of the move?

retired.why: one-sided (beyond_full on 90% of live reads) and no forward value (+0.0003); prorating made it more one-sided
retired.ask: Has today's range used under half, about all, or more than the expected move?

retired.why: fully determined by wall_return (NMI 0.72; its answer is a function of wall_return's)
retired.ask: Is a strike with a big pile of options close to price, or is there nothing heavy close by?

retired.why: NMI 0.66 with two_day_position; flipped at the same moments all day; the remainder adds nothing (+0.0005)
retired.ask: Is today an outlier against last night's close?

retired.why: folded in with its inside option split in two; JEV read back-inside-after-a-break as a live break on 3 of 12 before the split, 40 of 40 after
retired.ask: Where is price against the first half hour's range: inside all day, broken out, or back inside after a break?
